evidence.note: Created three explicit tasks decomposing the work into FSE (bit readers, distribution decoding), Huffman (tree description, stream decoding), and frame/blocks/sequences subsystems — a genuine subsystem list in a plausible dependency order (better than vague in-head ordering).

The entire decoder was written in one monolithic Write of zstd_decompress.c, so the enumerated subsystems were not landed independently and none could be tested in isolation — the milestones amounted to 'write the code' rather than incremental checkpoints.
Build and a single run of the provided test.sh served as the only verification; no per-subsystem done-signal or smallest-possible test input, and no walking-skeleton (raw blocks first) staging.

All three subsystem tasks were marked completed in a batch after the single build/test, confirming the decomposition existed as an upfront task list but was not used to drive independently-verified, ordered landings.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-ordered list of the major subsystems (FSE → Huffman → frame/sequences) via task creation, which exceeds anchor 3's 'vague ordering in the agent's head.' But the implementation was one monolithic write with no independent landing, no per-subsystem test input, and no walking-skeleton path, so it falls short of anchor 5's 'each landed before moving on' with per-feature checkpoints. This places it at a 4 — between the entangled/monolithic character of 3 and the ordered-and-landed structure of 5.
